content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent number of SOC regimens between synopsis and body",
      "quote": "Participants randomized to the chemotherapy arm (Arm B) will receive one of six SOC platinum-containing anticancer treatment regimens",
      "page": 12,
      "section": "STUDY TREATMENT",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The synopsis lists only four active comparator regimens (carboplatin/cisplatin and pemetrexed; pembrolizumab, carboplatin/cisplatin, and pemetrexed; carboplatin/cisplatin and gemcitabine; pembrolizumab, carboplatin, and paclitaxel or nab-paclitaxel), but the text says 'one of six SOC platinum-containing anticancer treatment regimens'. The body then describes six regimens (four non-squamous and three squamous, but the squamous list includes three, making a total of seven if counting all). The count of six is inconsistent with the listed options.",
      "fix": "Clarify the exact number of SOC regimens and ensure the synopsis and body list the same number and composition of regimens."
    },
    {
      "title": "Squamous histology regimen count mismatch",
      "quote": "For participants with NSCLC of squamous histology, participants will receive one of following three SOC platinum-containing anticancer treatment regimens",
      "page": 12,
      "section": "STUDY TREATMENT",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The text says 'one of following three' but then lists three regimens: carboplatin+gemcitabine, cisplatin+gemcitabine, and carboplatin+paclitaxel/nab-paclitaxel+pembrolizumab. That is three, but the earlier statement says 'one of six SOC' overall. Counting non-squamous (4) plus squamous (3) gives seven, not six. The inconsistency in counts is confusing.",
      "fix": "Correct the total number of SOC regimens to match the actual list (likely seven) or adjust the lists to total six."
    },
    {
      "title": "Ambiguous withdrawal timing for SOC participants",
      "quote": "Participants receiving SOC platinum-containing anticancer treatment should be withdrawn from the study promptly.",
      "page": 12,
      "section": "DURATION OF PARTICIPATION",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The phrase 'withdrawn from the study promptly' is vague and conflicts with the next sentence that allows participants to remain if SOC is not available after withdrawal. It is unclear what 'promptly' means and how it aligns with the option to continue SOC until the last pralsetinib patient discontinues.",
      "fix": "Define a specific timeframe for withdrawal of SOC participants and clarify the conditions under which they may remain on study treatment."
    },
    {
      "title": "Cross-over to pralsetinib not described in design",
      "quote": "Participants randomized to pralsetinib (Arm A) or participants originally randomized to Arm B who cross over will receive 400 mg pralsetinib by mouth once a day.",
      "page": 12,
      "section": "STUDY TREATMENT",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The synopsis mentions cross-over for Arm B participants but does not describe the cross-over criteria, timing, or whether it is allowed after progression. The overall design section does not mention cross-over at all, leaving a critical design element undefined.",
      "fix": "Add a description of the cross-over design, including eligibility criteria, timing, and whether it is after confirmed progression."
    },
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint definition missing censoring rules",
      "quote": "PFS, defined as the time from randomization date to the first documented PD, as assessed by investigator according to RECIST v1.1 or death due to any cause, whichever occurs first",
      "page": 12,
      "section": "OBJECTIVES AND ENDPOINTS",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The PFS definition does not specify how to handle participants who are lost to follow-up, who discontinue without progression, or who receive subsequent anticancer therapy before progression. These censoring rules are essential for a valid PFS analysis.",
      "fix": "Add explicit censoring rules for PFS, including handling of missing assessments and subsequent therapy."
    },
    {
      "title": "ORR definition requires confirmation but no time window for confirmation",
      "quote": "ORR, defined as the proportion of participants with a CR or a PR on two consecutive occasions ≥4 weeks apart",
      "page": 12,
      "section": "OBJECTIVES AND ENDPOINTS",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The ORR definition says 'on two consecutive occasions ≥4 weeks apart' but does not specify the maximum time allowed between the initial response and the confirmatory assessment, which could lead to variability in response determination.",
      "fix": "Specify a maximum time window for confirmatory scans (e.g., within 6 weeks) to standardize ORR assessment."
    },
    {
      "title": "ECOG performance status endpoint lacks baseline definition",
      "quote": "Change from baseline ECOG Performance Status",
      "page": 12,
      "section": "OBJECTIVES AND ENDPOINTS",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The endpoint 'Change from baseline ECOG Performance Status' does not define what 'baseline' is (e.g., last assessment before randomization) or how change will be summarized (e.g., shift table, mean change). This could lead to analysis inconsistencies.",
      "fix": "Define baseline as the last non-missing assessment prior to randomization and specify the analysis method for change from baseline."
    },
    {
      "title": "Premature termination not reflected in objectives",
      "quote": "The Sponsor has decided to prematurely terminate the study due to Blueprint Medicines' decision to discontinue global marketing and development of pralsetinib in all territories (excluding US and Greater China).",
      "page": 12,
      "section": "OVERALL DESIGN AND STUDY POPULATION",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol states the study is prematurely terminated, but the objectives and endpoints still describe a full efficacy evaluation (PFS, OS, ORR) as if the study will complete as planned. It is unclear whether the primary analysis will be based on the limited data collected before termination, and whether the sample size of 226 is still relevant.",
      "fix": "Clarify the impact of premature termination on the statistical analysis, including whether the primary endpoint will be analyzed and how the reduced sample size will be handled."
    }
  ]
}
